songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy set with debut The Other One and blazing Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: Featuring the historic first performance of The Other One and a soaring Turn On Your Lovelight, the show crackles with Jerry’s smoking guitar work. Pigpen’s organ drives the early jams while Phil delivers tight bass counterpoint. Excellent soundboard recordings capture every nuance, making it a standout snapshot of late‑1967.
ai_show_review.review:
The October 22, 1967 Winterland gig marks a pivotal moment in Dead history – it’s the night the band unveiled The Other One for the very first time. From the opening chords of Morning Dew to the psychedelic swirl of Cryptic Envelopment into that debut, the set builds with relentless momentum, peaking on a blistering turn of Turn On Your Lovelight and a rousing New Potato Caboose. Jerry Garcia’s guitar shreds with a smoking intensity that listeners still describe as “magmatic discharge,” while Pigpen’s organ adds a haunted depth to The Other One and fuels the bluesy swagger of It Hurts Me Too. Phil Lesh’s bass locks in tight, offering a sturdy counter‑point that pushes the jams forward, and Bob Weir provides solid rhythm work on Beat It On Down The Line. By the time the band returns to Cryptic Envelopment for the close, Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart are already clicking as a two‑drummer unit, laying down a tight groove that propels the final notes into a satisfying conclusion.

What makes this show especially compelling today is the quality of the surviving soundboard tapes. The Miller SBD (gd1967-10-22.sbd.miller.116257.flac16) has been remastered to astonishing clarity for a 1967 source – every guitar lick, organ swell, and drum nuance comes through crisp and clean. Coupled with the historic setlist and the band’s high‑energy execution, this recording stands out as an essential listen for anyone wanting to experience the Dead at the cusp of their psychedelic expansion.

best_recording.reason: Remastered soundboard capture with crystal‑clear mix that highlights the historic debut of The Other One and soaring Lovelight

key_highlights: Historic first performance of The Other One captured in pristine detail
Blazing Turn On Your Lovelight showcases Jerry’s smoking guitar work
New Potato Caboose delivers a tight, high‑energy jam with strong bass interplay
Excellent soundboard recordings provide remarkable clarity for a 1967 tape

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is on fire throughout, delivering smoking leads, shredding solos and a magmatic intensity especially on The Other One and Lovelight.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides tight counter‑point with confident bass lines that lock in with Jerry, driving the New Potato Caboose jam and supporting the extended improvisations.
band_performance.Bob: Weir lays down solid rhythm guitar and adds vocal strength on Beat It On Down The Line and contributes to the overall groove.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart makes his first recorded appearance, blending smoothly with Bill to create a cohesive two‑drummer foundation.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann holds the early groove steady, providing a solid rhythmic base that supports the high‑energy flow of the set.
